findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: query_techs, query_articles, get_article, get_domain_benchmark, get_cbam_timeline · Private data: query_telecom_expansion, query_companies, get_company, get_verified_suppliers, query_policies, get_policy, get_article, query_grades, get_grade, get_database_overview, compare_rcb, get_feedstock_overview, get_elt_recycling, query_trade_flows, get_trade_flow_summary, get_trade_dataset_overview, query_domain_benchmarks, get_domain_benchmark, get_cbam_timeline, get_battery_market_stats, get_constellation_status, query_spectrum_allocations, get_telecom_policy_timeline, calculate_recycled_content_gap, get_fitness_record, get_cn_eu_mapping · Public sink: query_techs, query_articles, get_article, get_rcb_index, get_grade_trend, query_trade_flows, get_trade_partner_ranking · Destructive: get_policy, get_article.

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
